unlockWhy: Families in the registry are encrypted — enter your password.
lead: The registry is the addresses of one area — e.g. a parish — and the families under them. Addresses are shared by everyone who runs the area; your browser encrypts the families' details with the area's key.
empty: The registry is empty. Add addresses one by one, a whole street at once, or paste a list in “Import and JSON”.

json.lead: Addresses with families and pastoral visits — for a copy, to correct by hand or with an AI. The import recognises addresses by their parts; it completes families.
json.readOnlyError: You can only read this registry.
json.description:
Address registry as JSON — format "{format}", version 1.

Document fields:
- format: always "recreatio/registry"
- areaName: name of the area (information only — the import goes to the area opened here)
- addresses[]: list of addresses
- addresses[].id: identifier of the place (from the export) — ignored on import; an address is recognised by its parts
- addresses[].address: the address as one text ("ul. Długa 5/3, 31-147 Kraków") OR an object with parts:
  street (street, without "ul."), house (house no.), unit (flat no.), locality (locality), district (district/estate),
  postcode (code "00-000"), post (post office). Each part may be empty; without a locality, the post office's locality counts.
- addresses[].household: the family at this address (optional; fields you don't give stay unchanged):
  family (family name, e.g. "Kowalscy"), people[] ({name, born "YYYY-MM-DD", note}), phone, email, notes, tags[] (labels),
  kolenda: { "YYYY": { status: {statuses}, date "YYYY-MM-DD", priest, note } }

Import: the same address (after normalising: letter case, Polish characters, "ul.") is the same place — it isn't created twice.
A family at an address that already has a family is completed. Family details are encrypted with the area's key in the browser.

How the app uses this data:
- The area's registry (“Registry and pastoral visit”) has the tabs Addresses, Pastoral visit, Import and JSON. Whoever reads the area reads it; whoever writes in it changes it.
- Addresses: places with families; search by address, surname and label ("tags").
- Pastoral visit: the year's visits from "kolenda" — filters Year, Status, Street, Day, Priest; “Plan” for the selected (day, priest); a list in order of day and address, “Print list”.
- Families and visits open only in a browser that has the area's key — search and filters work there too.
- Addresses are not encrypted. Their parts (streets, localities, districts, codes, post offices) are shared by the whole app: they also suggest the address in address questions in forms, on the person card and for the data controller.
- The import creates no appointments in the Calendar (the visit stays in the registry), no persons or accounts, and deletes nothing.

Example:
{sample}

plan.notDoc: This is not a registry document.
plan.twice: Entry {n}: the same address a second time ({address}) — merged with the earlier one.

noAreaKey: You don't have this area's key.

postal.unsure: Check the parts below — not everything in this address could be recognised unambiguously.
postal.noLocality: No locality — give it or the post office, so the street can be told apart from others with the same name.
postal.isLocality: “{street}” is a locality, not a street
